newsitem.title: UK: Britain considers dumping strict quarantine rules.
newsitem.headline: Britain considers dumping strict quarantine rules.

text.p: The new Labour government is considering replacing Britain's strict quarantine rules, an agriculture ministry spokeswoman said on Friday.
Pet owners have long campaigned for an end to the rules, under which warm-blooded animals -- from dogs to gerbils -- entering the island are kept in quarantine for six months.
The policy was introduced to stop rabies spreading from continental Europe but pet owners say it is cruel and prohibitively expensive to keep domestic animals locked up for so long.
"Ministers are going to be looking at the current situation. They have got to do a thorough investigation and take it from there," said the spokeswoman.
But she added: "The quarantine laws are as they are until we find a system that that is as safe and effective as the current one, which has kept Britain rabies-free for a quarter of a century."
There is no list of "leading contenders" to replace quarantine but options included vaccines and microchip implants that would track a pet's movements, she said.
The spokeswoman could not say when a decision might be taken, noting that Labour had only been in power for five weeks.
"Introduction (of a new system) will only be if and when cabinet ministers agree on a system that is going to keep the British public safe from rabies," she said.
